newsitem.title: USA: Andrews offers to combine Toy Biz and Marvel.
newsitem.headline: Andrews offers to combine Toy Biz and Marvel.

text.p: Financier Ronald Perelman's Andrews Group offered Tuesday to combine the operations of Toy Biz Inc. and Marvel Entertainment Group in a $350 million deal that would keep Perelman in control of more than 80 percent of Marvel.
Toy Biz is licensed to make toys based on Marvel's comic characters, which include X-Men, Spiderman and the Incredible Hulk.

The offer came as Marvel reported a third-quarter loss, as expected, of $12.5 million and warned of continuing losses in the current quarter as it suffers a drop in publishing, trading card and licensing revenues.
Marvel said a slump in publishing and trading card sales has forced it to consider a restructuring and other actions, which could result in substantial 1996 year-end charges.

Andrews last month agreed to acquire about 67 percent of Toy Biz's class A common stock from Isaac Perlmutter and Avi Arad, an Andrews spokesman said. Marvel currently holds all of Toy Biz's Class B common stock.
Toy Biz edged down 12.5 cents to $17.625 on the New York Stock Exchange at midday. Marvel fell $2 to $2.625, also on the NYSE.

Andrews, which is controlled by Perelman, already holds about 80.2 percent of Marvel's common stock. Perelman would maintain his stake in this deal, which would involve the issuance of 410 million new Marvel shares, a spokesman for Andrews said.
Slightly more than 100 million Marvel shares are outstanding, the spokesman said.

Marvel said separately that its loss, equal to 12 cents a share, in the third quarter ended Sept. 30, compared with profits of $19.6 million, or 19 cents a share, in the year-ago period. Revenues fell to $209.4 million from $269.0 million, partially offset by gains in toy and sticker sales.

As a result of continuing trends in its businesses, Marvel expects to report a loss of 25 cents to 30 cents a share for its fourth quarter ending Dec. 31, and a loss of 52 cents to 57 cents for full-year 1996.

The estimated 1996 loss is expected to include operating losses of $10 million-$15 million from Marvel Comics Group publishing and licensing operations, and a loss of $10 million-$15 million from Fleer/SkyBox trading card operations, the company said. It also includes an operating profit of $15 million-$20 million from the Panini international operation.
